sections.h2: Ottumwa and the Des Moines River
sections.html:
Ottumwa is the Wapello County seat in southeastern Iowa, and the Des Moines River splits it into north and south halves. The name comes from a Meskwaki word usually rendered as "tumbling waters," a nod to the rapids that once marked the site. A bridge replaced the old ferry by 1875, and South Ottumwa was annexed in the 1880s.

Coal, meatpacking and farm equipment built the town. The city peaked at 33,871 people in 1960, fell to 24,998 by 2000 and counted 25,529 in 2020. A city that has lost about a quarter of its peak population has a different housing market than a growing one, and prices reflect it.

sections.h2: Local jobs and what they mean for demand
sections.html: JBS Live Pork is the biggest employer with 2,550 jobs, followed by the Ottumwa Community School District at 800 and Ottumwa Regional Health Center at 692. John Deere Ottumwa Works adds 550. With a few large employers carrying the town, a change at one plant or at the school district shows up in local housing demand quickly.

sections.h2: Which side of the river is the house on?
sections.html:
The Ottumwa Community School District serves the city and rural Wapello County, and its elementary schools are grouped by north and south side. Douma and Liberty are on the south side, while James, Horace Mann, Wilson, Eisenhower and Fahrney are on the north. Check the attendance zone for your address before you describe it to a buyer.

U.S. Route 34 and Iowa Highway 149 serve the town, and U.S. 63 bypasses it. Amtrak's California Zephyr stops daily in each direction. Because the river divides the city, tell buyers which side the house sits on and how it connects to the highways. The Ottumwa Transit Authority runs five weekday routes and two Saturday routes, with no Sunday service.

The flood of 1851 damaged the town severely, and the Des Moines River still runs through the middle of it. Drainage and basements deserve a look before a sale. An owner who can show repair receipts has a clearer story for a buyer. Winters are cold, with an average January high of 32.0 degrees and annual snowfall of 23.6 inches, so roof and heating condition matter too.

sections.h2: Coal, packing plants and older housing
sections.html:
Coal mining began near Ottumwa by 1857, and clay and coal deposits in northeastern Wapello County fed early industry. The John Morrell and Company plant employed workers from 1877 to 1973, and JBS and John Deere carry on that industrial tradition today. Much of the housing stock grew up around those jobs, so many houses are decades old and carry the wear that comes with age.

Indian Hills Community College occupies the former Ottumwa Heights College campus, and Buena Vista University has a regional campus in the city. Those institutions give the town a steady base of renters and staff, and a landlord with a tired rental can find the market thin when selling the traditional way.

First, we ask for the address and basic facts: who owns it, whether it is occupied, what needs work and whether a mortgage or tax balance is attached. Second, we visit or review photos and run the title. Third, you get an offer in writing that you can take, counter or ignore.

If you accept, the title company opens an escrow file, confirms ownership and orders payoff letters. Closing day is a short signing. The deed goes to the county recorder with a declaration of value, and the transfer tax is handled at that point. Utilities and keys are the last items to settle.

Ottumwa requires rental housing to be registered and inspected once every three years, and about 2,600 rental units are registered. A rental permit starts with the Rental Permit Application, and the 2025 fee schedule is a separate PDF on the city's site.

The Building and Code Enforcement department, at 105 E. Third Street and 641-683-0650, handles complaints about tall grass and weeds, blighted properties and junk cars. A structure unfit for habitation gets a yellow placard on the front, and nobody may live in it until the violations are corrected. The Health Department posts a list of placarded houses.

Most new construction and remodeling projects need a building permit, and permits and inspection requests go through the city's online portal. The city enforces the 2015 International Property Maintenance Code. If a house has a placard, a cash buyer can still purchase it as-is, but ask the city what has to be fixed before anyone moves in again.

sections.h2: Wapello County property tax and transfer tax
sections.html:
Property tax is due in two halves, September 1 and March 1, and goes delinquent on October 1 and April 1. The Treasurer's office is in the courthouse at 101 W. 4th Street. Mailed checks must be postmarked by the end of the month to avoid the 1.5 percent penalty, and delinquent interest runs 1.5 percent per month.

Taxes unpaid as of May 1 get a publication fee and are advertised for the annual tax sale in June. Redemption interest is 2 percent per month, paid with certified funds.

The county recorder collects Iowa's transfer tax of $0.80 per $500, with the first $500 exempt, when the deed is presented. A declaration of value goes with the deed. The county keeps 17.25 percent of the receipts and the rest goes to the state.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or a placard
sections.html: If back taxes are due, they are paid from your proceeds at closing, so call the Treasurer for a current balance before you set a closing date. A vacant rental, an inherited house or a house with a yellow placard can all be sold as-is, though the placard stays with the property until the city signs off on repairs.

sections.h2: How a cash sale of an Ottumwa house works
sections.html:
Tell us the address and what shape the house is in. We take a look, and if the offer works for you, a title company writes up the deed and the payoff numbers. Nobody waits on a lender appraisal.

Gather the deed, your latest tax statement, mortgage payoff details and any city notices before closing. You choose the closing date, sign at the title company, and receive the remainder after liens and taxes are paid. That route suits an Ottumwa seller dealing with a placard, a vacant rental or an inherited house, since repairs and showings are not part of it.

faqs.q: How often are Ottumwa rentals inspected?
faqs.a: Once every three years. About 2,600 rental units are registered with the city.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Ottumwa?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $106,300 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $921.

faqs.q: When are Wapello County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1 and March 1, delinquent on October 1 and April 1. Delinquent interest is 1.5 percent per month.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Ottumwa house with a yellow placard?
faqs.a: Usually yes, as-is to a cash buyer, though no one can live in it until violations are corrected. Ask Building and Code Enforcement what is required before reoccupancy.

faqs.q: Who is the largest employer in Ottumwa?
faqs.a: JBS Live Pork with 2,550 jobs, followed by the Ottumwa Community School District at 800.
